title: AI flags Julie Knichel's brain hemorrhage before aneurysm treatment and her return to nursing
summary: Julie Knichel survived a ruptured aneurysm after AI-assisted detection and treatment, then returned to full-time nursing.
account: Julie Knichel, a 57-year-old nurse, suffered a ruptured brain aneurysm. At Baptist Health's Marcus Neuroscience Institute, AI reviewed her scan and alerted clinicians to the bleeding. They sealed the aneurysm with coils delivered through a catheter. After about three weeks in hospital, she recovered and returned to full-time nursing. Her symptoms began on February 2. The year is unspecified.
purpose: Detect brain hemorrhage and alert clinicians.

ratings.reason: Knichel survived a life-threatening hemorrhage and resumed her work and activities.

ai_role.statement: AI flagged the bleeding. Clinicians treated it. Neither the software nor its separate effect on survival is specified.

evidence.title: Stroke Nurse Shares Her Experience After Brain Aneurysm
evidence.quote: Ms. Knichel is happy to have returned to work full time and to her previous activities

must_hold: Prompt clinical review and access to aneurysm treatment.

headline: AI flags Julie Knichel's brain bleed before aneurysm treatment
